index.html.lede.1: Resin, block paving and full garden builds, within about twenty miles of Yeovil. Twenty-two years at it, no subcontractors, and a written quote with the materials named before anything is lifted.

index.html.p.1: Free, and no obligation. We come out and look before we price anything, and if we think the job is wrong for you we will say so.
index.html.p.2: A written quote with the materials named, so you can hold it against anybody else's. Not a range, and not a figure said at the door.
index.html.p.3: And we keep to it. Weather moves jobs sometimes; when it does you hear it from us before you hear it from anybody else.
index.html.p.4: Waste goes away under our own carrier licence. The site is swept at the end of every day, not just at the end of the job.

service.html.h1.1: What we lay, and what it costs
service.html.p.1: Stone aggregate mixed with a clear resin and trowelled out over a solid base. Smooth, water goes through it, and it is the finish most people have in mind when they say they want a resin drive.
service.html.p.2: It suits you if the base under your drive is still sound, you have had enough of weeds and loose stone, and the £70–£110 per square metre bracket is one you are happy with.
service.html.p.3: It does not suit you if the base has broken up. Resin is only as good as what sits under it, and laying it over a base that has already gone is the commonest way this job is wasted. If yours needs digging out we will tell you, and we will quote for that instead.
service.html.p.4: Individual blocks laid on sand over a compacted sub-base. The most forgiving surface there is: if a service has to come up in five years, the blocks lift and go back and nobody can tell.
service.html.p.5: Reckon on £60–£95 per square metre depending on the block. Allow for re-sanding the joints every few years — it is ten minutes with a brush, not a job.
service.html.p.6: Cheapest per square metre and much the quickest to lay. Right for a long farm or field access, where getting a vehicle up it matters more than how it looks.
service.html.p.7: A two-car drive is normally three to five working days: a day to dig out, a day for the sub-base, a day to lay, and a day either side for weather. The Sherborne drive took four.
service.html.p.8: We will not lay a new surface over a base we do not trust, and we do not take on fencing or tree surgery — somebody who does it every week will do it better. If a job is really one for somebody closer to you, we will say that too.
